title: VPC/Onprem GPU compatibility decision log + Terraform module notes
body:
Summary:
This is a working decision log + notes deck for VPC/on-prem GPU compatibility. Focus: concrete upgrade paths, Terraform module pinning strategy, validation harness commands, and explicit rollback/playbook sections for kube + NVIDIA driver + CUDA + NCCL changes. This doc is purposely informal — capture decisions, test outcomes, and open questions.

Scope:
- Target clusters: onprem-prod-01, onprem-stage-01, vpc-db-ml-01
- Hardware families: A100 (40GB), A10, T4 (legacy)
- Kubernetes ranges considered: 1.26 -> 1.30
- Goal: safe, repeatable upgrade path with Terraform-driven infra changes, and a validation script that runs as a post-upgrade gate.

Decision log (chronological):
- 2025-10-22: Choose GPU operator + nvidia-driver-installer DaemonSet managed by our Terraform module rather than baked AMIs. Rationale: easier driver rollout and rollback, fewer AMI permutations. (owner: Asha)
- 2025-11-05: Pin Terraform module gpu-operator to v2.1.0 for prod; allow v2.2.x in staging. Rationale: v2.2 has nontrivial CRD changes flagged in GH PR 76. (owner: Priya)
- 2025-11-18: Adopt two-stage driver rollout: stage nodes -> canary app -> full cluster. Add 48h observation window. (owner: Diego)
- 2026-01-09: For K8s 1.30 upgrade, require driver >= 535.x and CUDA >= 12.2. Decisions recorded here drive terraform variable defaults for 'gpu_driver_version' and 'cuda_toolkit_version'. (owner: Tom)

Compatibility matrix (summary — use as quick reference):
Columns: K8s | NVIDIA driver | CUDA | NCCL | GPU Operator | Notes
- 1.26 | 510.85 | 11.8 | 2.12 | 1.10.x | Baseline for T4; validated Nov-2025 on A10/T4
- 1.27 | 515.65 | 11.8 | 2.14 | 1.12.x | Minor NCCL fixes required for multi-GPU across MIG
- 1.28 | 520.61 | 11.8 / 12.1 | 2.14 | 1.14.x | CUDA 12.1 supported on A100, fallback to 11.8 for A10/T4
- 1.29 | 530.41 | 12.1 | 2.16 | 2.0.x | GPU-operator v2.0 introduces new webhook; requires additional RBAC in terraform module
- 1.30 | 535.104 | 12.2 | 2.18 | 2.1.x | Recommended for A100 40GB; T4 should remain on 11.8 in legacy pools

Notes on the matrix: these are conservative picks based on upstream release notes + our internal e2e runs. When we say 'validated' we mean: kube conformance smoke + perf microbench (token throughput test) ran successfully on a subset of nodes.

Validation harness (commands + checks):
- Pre-upgrade: curl node-exporter:9100/metrics -> confirm GPU memory free > 90% (no resident processes)
- Driver install dry-run: kubectl apply -f manifests/gpu-operator-vX-dryrun.yaml --server-dry-run=client
- Post-install checks (script snippets):
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu -> ensure 'Ready'
  - kubectl -n gpu-operator logs ds/nvidia-driver-installer | tail -n 200 -> check for 'installation complete'
  - kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].ready}' -> expect all true
  - nvidia-smi topo --matrix on host -> required for multi-GPU tests
  - run 'redwood-infra/tests/gpu_perf.sh --profile small' -> report must meet baseline (throughput >= 0.95x current baseline)

Terraform notes (module + variables + migration):
- Modules involved: infra/node-pools, infra/gpu-operator, infra/kubelet-config
- Versioning strategy: keep module tags immutable; create new module tag for each breaking GPU/operator change. Example: infra/gpu-operator v2.0.0 -> v2.1.0. Avoid in-place changes to module interfaces.
- Variables to pin in infra repo tfvars: 'gpu_operator_version', 'nvidia_driver_version', 'cuda_toolkit_version', 'node_ami_image'
- Migration example (staging -> prod):
  1) Bump infra/gpu-operator module in staging tfstate only. Run terraform plan and apply with 'parallelism=30' and 'target=module.gpu-operator'.
  2) Run post-deploy validation harness. Keep staging for 48h.
  3) If green, bump prod tfvars in a change that includes explicit 'driver_rollback_version' variable set.
- Terraform gotchas we hit:
  - Diffs caused by CRD schema changes can force unexpected deletes. Use 'kubectl apply -f crds.yaml' step outside of terraform when upgrading operator that changes CRD schema.
  - Provider timeouts: large clusters need provider configuration 'timeouts' increased for resource 'helm_release'.

Upgrade runbook (high-level):
1) Open ticket PD-XXXX, attach plan and GA matrix
2) Snapshot etcd and take core dumps backup
3) Cordone canary nodes (label gpu-upgrade=canary)
4) Apply module bump on canary subset via terraform with 'target=module.node-pool[canary]'
5) Wait till validation harness passes on canaries (smoke + perf small)
6) Gradually expand to remaining pools in waves (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 1 wave per 4 hours
7) After full rollout, monitor costs/latency/retry rate for 72h

Rollback playbook (fast):
- If more than 2 pods in core services fail with GPU OOM or driver API errors in a 30-min window, initiate rollback:
  1) Set terraform var 'nvidia_driver_version' to 'driver_rollback_version' and apply to node-pools (targeted).
  2) Restart kubelet on affected nodes (systemctl restart kubelet) to ensure old driver modules are restored (in our operator flow the driver installer will run with the pinned version).
  3) If pods still crash, cordon node and migrate workloads off, then reprovision node (terraform taint + apply).
  4) Post-mortem: collect dmesg, journalctl -u kubelet, and gpu-operator logs. Create incident ticket and attach artifacts.

Testing matrix and thresholds (what 'green' looks like):
- Smoke: all GPU nodes Ready and nvidia-smi shows at least one process state = 0 (no zombies).
- Perf: latency p95 for INF model < 1.25x baseline, throughput >= 0.95x baseline for batch size used in test.
- Stability: no node reboot or kernel oops in 48h; pod restart rate < 0.5% across all ML deployment pods.

Known issues and mitigations observed in prior upgrades:
- CRD migrations in GPU-operator v2.0 caused helm_release diff churn; workaround: apply CRD manifests separately and wait 10m before changing helm release.
- NCCL 2.18 on older kernels produced 'missed heartbeat' in daisy-chained nvlink topologies; mitigation: pin NCCL to 2.16 for those pools, open ticket with vendor.
- Kubelet cgroup driver mismatches surfaced only after driver upgrade; ensure kubelet cgroup driver config is validated by infra/kubelet-config module preflight.

Open questions (priority ordering):
- Q1: Do we standardize on CUDA 12.x across all new pools, or keep mixed CUDA families by hardware? (P1 for infra)
- Q2: Should we make driver rollback automatic in terraform via a "preflight-check" hook or keep manual to avoid accidental rollbacks? (security review required)
- Q3: Is it worth investing in a canary pool with mixed hardware types for broader validation coverage?

Action items:
- Priya: draft PR to add 'driver_rollback_version' variable and docs to infra module (due 2026-02-24)
- Diego: add CRD apply step to CI pipeline and test with gpu-operator v2.0 in sandbox (due 2026-02-28)
- Asha: finalize perf baseline script and add to redwood-infra / tests (due 2026-03-05)

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets
- Re-run driver installer on node: kubectl -n gpu-operator exec ds/nvidia-driver-installer -- /usr/local/bin/driver-installer --reinstall
- Inspect kernel module list: ssh node && sudo lsmod | grep nvidia
- Force kubelet to resync: sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sleep 30 && journalctl -u kubelet -n 200

References:
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/gpu-operator/compare/v1.14...v2.0
- Nvidia release notes: developer.nvidia.com/cuda-release-notes
- Internal ticket track: PD-4123 (upgrade experiments, logs attached)

Notes to self: Keep this doc short and link to larger playbooks in Confluence. This is the live decision log for infra and SRE to reference when planning the next 1-2 upgrades.
